title: Sold to the Back Row
cues: Alright, y'all, sit down, sit down.
Dim, worn wooden chairs in a dusty, sun-drenched hall
intro_or_break
Lot number one. Somebody start me at fifty.
A gleaming brass gavel rising from a velvet cushion
intro_or_break
Bang.
A flash of white, a burst of shimmering heat haze
intro_or_break
County fair in August and the heat is on the tin
Golden sunlight spills over a Ferris wheel, blurred motion
intro_or_break
Got a gavel in my fist and a toothpick in my grin
A dark silhouette gripping a polished wooden gavel, a tiny flame
intro_or_break
Granddaddy was an auctioneer, he taught me how to talk
Ethereal hands of an older man, guiding a younger one
drive
Said the money's in the mouth, so make the mouth outrun the clock
A swirling vortex of coins and shadows, a speeding clock
drive
Front row full of farmers fanning faces with the flyers
Farmers in the foreground, a flurry of bright paper wings
drive
Back row full of cousins and a couple certified liars
Dark figures in the background, leaning in, a knowing smirk
drive
First lot's a riding mower, only runs if you push it
A rusted riding mower, motionless, a single dark shadow
drive
Second lot's a recliner and my Uncle Hollis is still in it
A plush recliner, a ghostly form slumped within, faded fabric
drive
Third lot's a church organ, only plays a single key
A grand, stationary church organ, one illuminated key glows
drive
Hold it down long enough and it sounds like Sunday to me
Slow motion: a hand holding a key, the echoes of hymns
drive
Lady in the visor got her paddle in the air
A woman's visor, a frantic swat at a buzzing insect
drive
She was swatting at a wasp, but I'm counting it, I don't care
Blurred motion of a hand counting, a focused gaze
drive
Going once! (Going once!)
A rising wave of dark hands, a rhythmic, echoing call
drive
Going twice! (Going twice!)
Repeating dark hands, a building wave of intensity
drive
Sold to the back row, pay me the price
A shadowed hand takes a goat, a quiet transaction
drive
Keep your hands down, don't you scratch your nose
Silhouetted hands remain still, a hesitant, watchful pose
drive
Scratch it at my auction and you bought a goat
Dark hands scratch, a quick, furtive movement, a shadowed face
drive
Sold! (Sold!) Sold to the back row!
Crimson spotlights flash across a surging, shadowy crowd, arms raised in fervent, silent calls
drive
Riding mower who'll gimme fifty gimme sixty gimme seventy it's missing every blade but it's a beauty
A rusted red riding mower spins wildly, blades slicing through a haze of golden dust
drive
Got a bid up in the bleachers from a preacher in a camo hat who's bidding like it is his Christian duty
Silhouette figures in camo hats rise from the bleachers, hands gesturing dramatically upwards
drive
Then the recliner with my uncle in it hundred hundred twenty hundred forty and he's sleeping like a tractor
A plush, worn recliner sits bathed in amber light, a dark, still figure slumbers deeply
drive
Sold for one-sixty to a lady with a lanyard and she's rolling him away and he's waving like an actor
A woman in a lanyard pulls a shadowed figure away, he waves enthusiastically from afar
drive
Church organ only plays a B flat but it's holy and I'm selling it for ninety to the preacher with a nod
A grand, glowing organ dominates a dark space, notes ripple out in ethereal blue light
drive
He's been bidding on everything and I'm thinking that the camo is a costume and the preacher is a fraud
A shadowed figure in a camo hat studies the crowd with suspicion, a ripple of doubt forms
drive
Bidding is bouncing from a bucket hat to a cowboy hat to a baby in a stroller with a bottle in the air
A chaotic tumble of hats – a bucket, cowboy, baby – spins and bounces with joyful motion
drive
Hold up the baby didn't bid but mama nodded so I'm counting it and selling her a tire and a folding chair
A mother nods approvingly as she accepts a tire and folding chair with a knowing smile
drive
Clicking it ticking it picking it flipping it selling it telling it sold to the corner with the coupon and the cane
Rapid clicks and ticks flicker with a frantic, pulsing, neon blue light illuminating a corner
drive
Paddles are flapping and grandmas are clapping and somebody's cattle are laughing and the sky's about to rain
Flapping paddles and clapping hands surround a churning, grey sky, heavy with impending rain

Lot forty-seven.
A single, weathered goat stands alone in a dusty paddock, illuminated by a single spotlight
drive
A goat. His name is Deacon.
A small, brown goat with pleading eyes stares out from the darkness, a single shadow looming large
drive
He bites. He sings. He's been to county jail. Twice.
A dark silhouette of a biting goat sings a haunting, off-key melody
drive
Starting bid. Somebody. Anybody. Please take Deacon.
Empty bleachers and a single spotlight fall on the goat, a desperate plea hangs in the air

drive

Now Deacon's eating on a sun hat and he's singing in the key of B flat with the organ that I sold to the preacher in the

The goat kicks wildly, biting hands, a large gavel slams down in a burst of white light
drive
Hold on. He got my gavel. Shit.
Silence. A single, dark hand clutches a heavy gavel, shadows deepen around the scene
